questions.stem: Why are metals malleable (can be hammered into shape)?

options.text: Metallic bonds are weak and break when force is applied
Metal atoms are very small and can be pushed past each other
Layers of metal ions can slide over each other while the delocalised electrons maintain the bonding
The lattice structure has large gaps that allow movement

questions.explanation: Metals are malleable because layers of metal ions can slide over each other when a force is applied. The delocalised electrons move with the ions and continue to hold the structure together, so the metallic bonding is maintained throughout. The metal changes shape but does not break.
